- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.5) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices during early periods of strong sentiment (e.g., sentiment >0.6) — model is too conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment spikes, often missing the peak or delaying correction.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp declines, pushing prices too low when sentiment is recovering.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising, then underestimate later when sentiment stabilizes or declines.
- When sentiment is low (<0.3), model tends to underestimate, but fails to recognize potential rebound — underestimates the “bottom” before reversal.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment is diverging — e.g., if price is rising but sentiment is falling, model may continue trend instead of adjusting.
